findings.title: User-level download/upload over plaintext HTTP to apo-games.de (MITM/malicious-server controlled)
findings.code_excerpt:
public final static String USERLEVELS_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoSn4ke/get_level.php";
public final static String USERLEVELS_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoSn4ke/save_level.php";
findings.entry_point: Network: any on-path attacker (ARP/DNS spoof, rogue AP) or the apo-games.de server itself. Auto-triggered at app start: ApoSnakePanel.init() (ApoSnakePanel.java:58-64) spawns a thread -> ApoSnakeUserlevels.loadUserlevels() (ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:22-38) -> ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.load() (ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:153-217).
findings.sink: URLConnection to http://www.apo-games.de/... ; response consumed line-by-line via input.readLine() in load() (ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:179-207); uploads via printout.writeBytes(content) in save() (ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:130-135).
findings.data_path: ApoSnake.isOnline() gate (ApoSnake.java:48-53) -> new URL(USERLEVELS_GETPHP).openConnection() -> DataInputStream(urlConn.getInputStream()) -> readLine() loop stores every 11th line as a level string (levels.add(str), line 184) -> returned via getLevels() -> ApoSnakeUserlevels.getAllLevelsSorted() -> static ApoSnakeLevel.editorLevels (ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:30) -> played via ApoSnakeMenu.touchedButton("userlevels") (ApoSnakeMenu.java:75-77).
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker on the same LAN (coffee-shop WiFi) ARP-spoofs the device and answers DNS for www.apo-games.de, or compromises the apo-games.de host. Every ApoSnake client that launches while 'online' fetches its community level list from the attacker, who can serve arbitrary level strings and forged rating statistics (fun/easy/hard counts, Float/Integer.valueOf-parsed at ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:186-204). Uploaded player levels are likewise sent in cleartext and can be read/tampered in transit.
findings.preconditions: Device considers itself online (ConnectivityManager, ApoSnake.java:40-41); attacker needs a network vantage point or control of the server. Cleartext must be permitted: manifest (AndroidManifest.xml) sets minSdkVersion 8 and no usesCleartextTraffic attribute, so HTTP works by default on all Android versions below API 28; on Android 9+ the OS blocks this request outright.
findings.validation_plan: Install the APK on an API <= 27 emulator. Redirect www.apo-games.de to a local host (adb shell settings / hosts via remount, or run mitmproxy in transparent mode on the emulator network). tcpdump shows the POST body 'level=...' in cleartext to port 80. Serve a canned get_level.php response (see ApoSnake-02 for the required 11-line format) and observe the injected level become playable under the in-game 'userlevels' button.

findings.title: Server-supplied level string parsed with no bounds/format checks: negative/huge array allocation and out-of-bounds reads crash the app
findings.entry_point: The level string downloaded from get_level.php (stored via levels.add(str) in ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:184, copied into ApoSnakeLevel.editorLevels in ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:30). Reached when the player taps the 'userlevels' menu button: ApoSnakeMenu.java:76 -> ApoSnakePanel.setPuzzleGame (136-147) -> ApoSnakePuzzleGame.loadLevel (125-223). Also reached with locally edited strings, but the remote path requires no device access.
findings.sink: new int[height][width] at line 161 and l.charAt(y * level[0].length + x + 2) at lines 167/195 - allocation size and string indices are computed directly from unvalidated bytes of the server line. Header chars < 96 yield negative dimensions; chars up to 0xFFFF yield dimensions up to ~65k x 65k; body length is never compared to width*height.
findings.data_path: HTTP line -> ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.load() (11-line grouping; only the level line is attacker-arbitrary, metadata lines must be numeric or the load aborts safely) -> ApoSnakeUserlevels.sortByUpload()/getAllLevelsSorted() (ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:59-78, 44-57; built-in duplicates filtered by ApoSnakeLevel.isIn, everything else kept) -> ApoSnakeLevel.editorLevels[p[0]] (ApoSnakePuzzleGame.java:152) -> loadLevel() parse, executed on the render/think thread; no try/catch anywhere on this path.
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker uploads (see ApoSnake-03, no account needed) or MITM-injects a level line such as "\u1000\u1000" + filler with numeric metadata around it. Every client listing that level allocates int[4000][4000] (~64 MB -> OutOfMemoryError on era-typical small Dalvik heaps) or, with a header like "AB", throws NegativeArraySizeException, or with a short body throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at line 167. The uncaught exception kills the game process; because levels are re-downloaded on every start, tapping 'userlevels' keeps crashing the app until the poison level disappears from the server.
findings.preconditions: Attacker-controlled level string present in the get_level.php response (via upload endpoint or MITM from ApoSnake-01); player taps 'userlevels'. Metadata lines of the 11-line group must parse as numbers (Float/Integer.valueOf) or loadUserlevels()'s catch(Exception) (ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:34) aborts before editorLevels is set. Impact limited to process death/OOM - no evidence of memory corruption (Java arrays are bounds-checked), so no RCE.
findings.validation_plan: Run a fake get_level.php (enabled via ApoSnake-01 setup) returning exactly 11 lines: line0='AB', lines1-3='0', line4='name', lines5-10='0'. Launch app, tap 'userlevels': logcat shows NegativeArraySizeException at ApoSnakePuzzleGame.java:161 and the process exits. Repeat with line0='zz'+short body -> StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at line 167; with line0 containing two '\u1000' chars -> OutOfMemoryError at line 161.

findings.title: Unauthenticated, unsigned level upload endpoint lets anyone publish content pushed to all players
findings.entry_point: In-game editor 'upload' button: ApoSnakeEditor.touchedButton (ApoSnakeEditor.java:186-196) -> uploadString() (227-234) -> ApoSnakeUserlevels.addLevel (ApoSnakeUserlevels.java:84-91) -> save(). Any HTTP client can hit save_level.php directly with the same one-parameter form body.
findings.sink: POST http://www.apo-games.de/apoSn4ke/save_level.php (URL taken from ApoSnakeConstants.java:6) with body 'level=<arbitrary string>' - no authentication, no per-user identity, no signature, no client-side sanity limit beyond the editor UI's own 14x14 cap (ApoSnakeEditor.java:202,210), which a direct HTTP caller ignores entirely.
findings.data_path: Editor grid -> getLevelString() (ApoSnakeEditor.java:240-257 builds '<w><h><cells>' from raw ints) -> addLevel() duplicate-check against already-downloaded levels only -> save() writes the string verbatim (only URLEncoder.encode applied) to the PHP script. The server's response is discarded; whatever was accepted later comes back to every client through get_level.php and feeds ApoSnake-02's parser.
findings.attack_scenario: An attacker scripts curl --data 'level=<crafted payload>' against save_level.php (endpoint discoverable from any APK string table; the obfuscated path segment 'apoSn4ke' provides no secrecy). Poisoned levels persist server-side and are served to the whole player base on next fetch, enabling the remote-crash scenario of ApoSnake-02 or mass garbage-content injection, with no attribution or revocation mechanism in the protocol.
findings.preconditions: save_level.php still live and accepting anonymous submissions (server-side condition outside this codebase); for the in-app path, device online and editor level test-solved (setLevelSolved, ApoSnakeEditor.java:70-76 gates the upload button).
findings.validation_plan: From a PC: curl -d 'level=ABxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx' http://www.apo-games.de/apoSn4ke/save_level.php, then curl -d 'Get=' http://www.apo-games.de/apoSn4ke/get_level.php and grep for the submitted string. If the service is dead, reproduce locally by pointing ApoSnakeConstants.java:5-6 at a stub PHP/Flask pair implementing the same contract and replaying the flow from the app.

findings.title: Level-progression flag stored as plain int in SharedPreferences; trivially editable to unlock all levels
findings.entry_point: Local XML file /data/data/net.apogames.aposnake/shared_prefs/ApoSnakePref.xml (created in ApoSnake.onCreate via getSharedPreferences(ApoSnakeConstants.PREFS_NAME, 0), ApoSnake.java:43; PREFS_NAME defined in ApoSnakeConstants.java:11).
findings.sink: settings.getInt("solved", 0) -> solvedLevel(int) (ApoSnakePanel.java:179-181) -> ApoSnakePuzzleChooser.setSolved (ApoSnakePuzzleChooser.java:66-79): the only guard is clamping to MAX_LEVELS-1, there is no integrity check, and the same value is written back unconditionally in savePreferences (ApoSnakePanel.java:72-77).
findings.data_path: Edited 'solved' value in the prefs XML -> loadPreferences() during init (ApoSnakePanel.java:64) -> setSolved marks all buttons solved and persists via savePreferences -> puzzle chooser exposes every level (touchedPressed loops i <= this.solved, ApoSnakePuzzleChooser.java:84-88). No server-side or cryptographic validation exists anywhere in the variant (grep: no MessageDigest/Cipher in src/).
findings.attack_scenario: A rooted user (or adb backup, since android:allowBackup is unset and defaults to permissive on relevant APIs) edits ApoSnakePref.xml to '<int name="solved" value="99" />'; on next launch all 29 built-in levels are selectable and marked solved. Purely a cheating vector - no code execution, affects only single-player progression.
findings.preconditions: Root access to the device or ability to extract/restore app-private storage; no network involvement.
findings.validation_plan: On a rooted emulator: adb root; adb shell 'echo "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"utf-8\" standalone=\"yes\" ?><map><int name=\"solved\" value=\"28\" /></map>" > /data/data/net.apogames.aposnake/shared_prefs/ApoSnakePref.xml'; relaunch the app and observe all level-chooser circles unlocked/green in the puzzle chooser screen.

categories_checked_and_absent: remote_code_loading - no ClassLoader/defineClass/System.load/loadLibrary anywhere in src/ or gen/ (grepped); libs/bitsengine.jar contains only engine rendering/input classes, no loader
untrusted_deserialization - no ObjectInputStream/XML decoder; the only inbound stream is readLine()-parsed text (ApoSnakeUserlevelsLoad.java:179-207)
weak_integrity_check - no MessageDigest/MD5/hash usage of any kind in this variant, unlike sibling variants
path_traversal - no java.io.File, no getExternalStorage/user.home/user.dir usage; only persistence is SharedPreferences
legacy_sandbox_assumption - no applet entry point; single LAUNCHER activity (AndroidManifest.xml)
credential_or_secret_exposure - no credentials, tokens or secrets embedded; requests carry no auth material at all
information_disclosure - uploads contain only the level grid string; nothing identifying the device/user is transmitted
notes: Source root corpus/android/ApoSnake resolves to apogames/Android/ApoSnake; all 21 Java files (19 src + generated R/BuildConfig) were opened. This is the smallest-risk shape seen in the corpus family: the Android port dropped the desktop shared stack (ApoClassLoader, ApoIO, AppletHighscore, .cheat/.mar/.rep formats) entirely - there is NO custom class loading, NO binary save/replay parsing, and NO hashing here. Attack surface collapses to: (1) the clone-family UserlevelsLoad/Userlevels/Constants trio talking plaintext HTTP (findings 01-03 form one causal chain: anonymous upload -> server persistence -> download -> unvalidated parser -> crash/OOM), and (2) an unprotected local progress pref (04). Note the parser in ApoSnakePuzzleGame.loadLevel (header-derived dimensions at lines 159-161, unchecked charAt at 167/195) is the same design pattern as sibling variants' level loaders, so the flaw likely propagates across clones even where the transport differs. Also noteworthy: minSdkVersion 8 plus absent android:usesCleartextTraffic means the HTTP traffic only becomes OS-blocked on Android 9+, i.e., the exposure window covers the entire historical install base; BuildConfig.DEBUG=true indicates these sources build as debuggable artifacts.
